headline: UK Department For Work And Pensions Offline After Cyber Incident
seoTitle: DWP Cyber Incident and Benefits Systems Offline
metaDescription: The UK Department for Work and Pensions has suspended online benefit and pension services following a cyber incident, though payments continue as normal.
aiSummaryBullets: The Department for Work and Pensions deactivated online portals for benefits and pensions following a serious cyber security incident.
Government officials confirmed that despite the service outage, regular benefit and pension payments are currently continuing to be processed.
The National Cyber Security Centre is currently investigating the incident with no evidence found that personal user data has been compromised.
aiContextParagraph: On November 27, 2026, the United Kingdom's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) experienced a significant cyber incident that forced the temporary suspension of various online services. Affected systems include those used for processing Universal Credit, Personal Independence Payment (PIP), and state pensions. Government ministers and the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) have initiated an investigation into the nature of the disruption. While online account access and new application processing faced interruptions as a precautionary security measure, authorities have stated there is currently no evidence that sensitive personal data has been accessed or compromised. Official reports indicate that regular payments to claimants are proceeding as scheduled despite the technical downtime. Government departments are currently monitoring the situation to determine if other areas of public infrastructure were targeted, though no evidence of broader impact has been identified at this time.
whyItIsViral: This story is trending due to coverage by eight independent news outlets and a very high velocity of reporting across national and international media.
